_comment: Person D's fake /ask payloads. Three cases on purpose: a clean multi-hop success, a resolved source-conflict, and an iteration-capped partial answer. Building the UI against only the happy path means the conflict and partial states never get built until it is too late. Conflict shape follows docs/contracts.md (multi-claim), NOT the older pairwise claim_a/claim_b shape in the fixtures PDF.

clean_answer_example.question: Which war was won by the organization that included Isolde Mournvale as one of its members?
clean_answer_example.answer: The War of Drowned Light. Isolde Mournvale is a sworn member of the Ashen Order [isolde_mournvale.md], and the Ashen Order won the War of Drowned Light in 358 AS [annals_of_the_ashen_era_vol2.pdf, p.47].

conflict_answer_example.question: In which year was the Gauntlet of Sorrowfell actually forged?
conflict_answer_example.answer: 341 AS, according to the official codex record naming forge-master Kellan Ashgrove [annals_of_the_ashen_era_vol1.pdf, p.112]. Note: a personal letter gives a different, hedged year of approximately 312 AS [letter_gravemaw_sighting.txt, p.2]. We favour the codex because it is an official, specific record with a named forge-master, while the letter itself expresses uncertainty about its own claim.

citations.claim: Forged in 341 AS by Kellan Ashgrove
citations.text: Artifact: Gauntlet of Sorrowfell | Forged: 341 AS | Forge-master: Kellan Ashgrove | Attunement cost: 3 shards of will
They say the Gauntlet of Sorrowfell was forged in the winter of 312 AS, though old Harrow always claimed it was closer to 300, back before the Order even had a name.

conflicts.resolution: Codex preferred: higher reliability tier (T1 over T4), more specific record (names the forge-master and the exact year), and the letter hedges its own claim.
